(2) `sendDrop` becomes `internalMutation({ args: { mailLogId: v.id("mailLog") } })`: row must be claimed else return null; re-run `alertGate` (send-time recheck) and the watch/inbox checks; on refusal patch `{ status: "suppressed", reason, error: message }`; else `const { outboundId } = await agentmail.sendMessage(ctx, {...fixed subject/body + footer line `Unsubscribe: ${process.env.CONVEX_SITE_URL}/alerts/unsubscribe?token=${await tokenFor(ctx, userId)}`})` then patch `{ status: "queued", outboundId, attempt: 0, nextCheckAt: now + BACKOFF_MS[0] }` and `ctx.scheduler.runAfter(BACKOFF_MS[0], internal.notify.reconcileDrop, { mailLogId, attempt: 1 })` in the same transaction; if sendMessage throws, patch `{ status: "failed", reason: "send_failed", error: sanitizeError(err) }`. decisions_needed: D64 Adopt @convex-dev/rate-limiter (not installed today; guidelines recommend it) for auth attempts, auth mail sends, inbox provisioning and drop rechecks; test harness registers it per D51.

D65 Auth mail (verification + reset codes) is sent through the Convex Auth Password provider's verify/reset Email hooks using AgentMail REST from ALERTS_INBOX_ID; no new mail vendor, no custom token crypto; 8-digit numeric codes, 15-minute expiry, 3 sends/hour/address, 200/hour global (subject to scope question 1).

D66 Existing accounts are not grandfathered as verified: the provider's own `verify && !emailVerified` path forces a code on next sign-in; alerts stay suppressed (reason unverified, visible in-app) until then.

D67 Email normalisation = trim + lowercase + format check + 254-char cap; no plus/dot folding (documented limitation: aliases are distinct accounts; per-mailbox abuse bounded by the global drop_email switch and per-address auth-mail limits).

D68 notify.sendDrop becomes an internalMutation (enqueue + queued + schedule in one transaction), mirroring drafts.approveAndSend; mailStatus gains `unknown` and `suppressed` with a `reason`; cap/no-email/not-configured suppressions move from failed+error to suppressed+reason (tests updated accordingly).

D69 Late bounce/complaint propagation via the AgentMail component `onEvent` hook; a bounce or complaint suppresses the address (alertSettings.suppressedReason) until the user re-enables; complaint counts as delivered-then-flagged.
D70 mailLog dedupe rows in transient states (send_failed, caps, not_configured) are re-claimable after 24h; opted_out/deleted/address_suppressed are never re-claimed.

D71 Market history state machine (not_configured/queued/running/success/empty_result/retryable_failure/terminal_failure), transactional claim in requestLookup, 3 attempts with 10m/1h/6h backoff, manual refresh of a success only after 7 days, migration of legacy stamps via migrateStamps after deploy.

D72 Dashboard canonical counting: a watch with purchaseId contributes nothing to sources/activity (the purchase item carries its history); per-currency bests; truncation flags rendered as 'recent' labels.

D73 Reactive queries take a coarse `now` argument (5-minute steps) for display-only computations; mutations keep their own clock for eligibility; STALE_PRICE_MS = 3 days makes a price 'may be out of date' and forces verdict unknown.
D74 Cron fairness: items get nextCheckAt (rotation like sweep) and a per-user slice per tick (10) for both priceWatch.runAll and watches.sweep; open-claim check via claims.by_item_kind_status.

D75 Retention policy: processedEvents.payload cleared after 30 days for terminal rows; observational checks older than 180 days pruned keeping newest 30 per parent and any check referenced by a claim; mailLog sent/failed/suppressed pruned after 90 days; ledger/claims/drafts/replies/purchases never pruned; resumable 200-doc pages every 6h.
D76 Global caps added: claim_email 100/day and inbound_extract 500/day (inbound refusals become needs_review, retried hourly); charge() enforces any global entry.

D77 Account deletion = confirmation phrase + session revocation + tombstone (accountState) + resumable purge children-first + AgentMail inbox deletion with 5 bounded retries; tombstone row persists; all scheduled readers skip tombstoned users.
